title: Afcons Infrastructure Ltd. v. Cherian Varkey Construction

content.caseIdentity: Afcons Infrastructure Ltd. v. Cherian Varkey Construction, (2010) 8 SCC 24
content.facts: Cochin Port Trust construction work was subcontracted by Afcons to Cherian Varkey. The subcontract contained no arbitration clause. In a recovery suit, the trial court referred the dispute to arbitration under Section 89 CPC despite the defendants' objection.
questionsBeforeCourt: What procedure should a civil court follow under Section 89 CPC and Order X Rule 1A?
Can a civil court refer a suit to arbitration under Section 89 CPC without consent of all parties?
content.ratioDecidendi: Section 89 CPC must be applied practically after pleadings are complete and before framing issues; the court should identify the nature of the dispute, explain the ADR options and take the parties' preferences. Where there is no pre-existing arbitration agreement, a reference to arbitration under Section 89 requires consent of all parties. The court cannot compel unwilling parties into arbitration.
content.holding: The trial court and High Court erred in referring the dispute to arbitration without the parties' agreement. The appeal was allowed and the arbitration reference was set aside.
content.relevance: Leading Supreme Court authority on the operation of Section 89 CPC, ADR selection, and the requirement of party consent for arbitration under Section 89.

sources.evidence: Judgment identifies Civil Appeal No.6000 of 2010, parties and judgment dated 26 July 2010; paras 15-16 explain the practical Section 89 procedure; paras 23-26 address consent and ADR; para 35 answers the questions and para 36 sets aside the arbitration reference.
Later Supreme Court judgment expressly relies on Afcons for the proposition that arbitration under Section 89 requires consent of the parties.
